noticeAddresses.name: SK University Hills Owner MZL, LLC

term.value: Lease 11/10/2015; commenced 8/18/2016; original term to 8/31/2026. Tenant exercised the 1st Extension via the 2nd Amendment, so the current term runs to 8/31/2031. Remaining: an 'Extra Period' (fraction of a year to Jan 31) plus the 2nd–5th Extension Periods (the 5th was added by the 2nd Amendment).

optionNotes: Four 5-year renewal options on 6 months' notice, PLUS a 5th Extension Period added by the 2nd Amendment (5/30/2025) at $502,062/yr ($22/SF), on the same notice terms. The 1st Extension (9/1/2026–8/31/2031) was exercised in the 2nd Amendment. There is also an 'Extra Period' (a fraction of a year ending the January 31 after the then-current term expires), at the rate in effect immediately prior.

percentageRent.value: 2% of the Gross Sales for each lease year (Feb 1–Jan 31) in excess of a NATURAL breakpoint. The breakpoint ('Breaking Point') = the annual minimum rent for that lease year ÷ .02 — so it floats up with each rent step (e.g. $365,136 ÷ .02 = $18,256,800 in the first period; $387,957 ÷ .02 = $19,397,850 at $17/SF). Prorated for lease years over/under 365 days. Reported within 120 days after each lease year; LL audit right (tenant pays audit cost if sales understated ≥4%).

exclusives.description: No other premises in the SC may contain more than 15,000 SF used for the sale/display of off-price brand-name men's, women's and children's apparel. Exceptions: TJ Maxx, Marshalls (and affiliates); Wal-Mart, Target, JCPenney, Sears, Kohl's (with an Alternate-Rent / termination mechanic if Kohl's opens) and other 50,000+ SF general-merchandise department stores; a full-line sporting goods store; and rights granted to tenants existing as of the lease date.

goDark.value: Per the 2nd Amendment (§6), Section 4.8 was REPLACED: if the Premises are closed for business for 180 consecutive days or more (after the 1st anniversary of the Commencement Date), other than for a Force Majeure Event, Landlord may terminate on 30 days' notice (before Tenant gives notice it will reopen). If Tenant gives a reopen notice it must reopen within 90 days. No continuous-operation covenant otherwise.

assignment.value: No Landlord consent required to assign or sublet the Premises; Landlord consent IS required to assign/sublet more than 25% of the floor area. Tenant may assign/sublet to a Related Party without consent and without giving Landlord a termination right.

camTax.value: CAM: Pro-rata = Ground Floor Area of Premises ÷ Total Gross Leasable Area of the SC; service areas excluded; no admin fee; LL insurance, management/admin/overhead and capital expenditures EXCLUDED; CAP — 1st year ≤ $1.19/SF, thereafter increases ≤ 4%/yr non-cumulative (excl. snow removal and utility-rate increases); audit within 3 years. Taxes: same pro-rata; separately-assessed out-parcels excluded from the denominator; initial estimate $3.73/SF; audit within 3 years.

leaseNotes.label: Security Deposit
leaseNotes.value: None

leaseNotes.label: Use Clause
leaseNotes.value: Retail store (no narrow use restriction). Operating covenant is one business day only: Tenant must open fully fixtured as a T.J. Maxx, Marshalls or HomeGoods by the later of 90 days after the Commencement Date or the first Opening Day, and remain open at least one business day; nothing requires Tenant to operate under any particular name or stay open thereafter.

leaseNotes.label: Radius
leaseNotes.value: None

leaseNotes.label: LL Radius
leaseNotes.value: None

leaseNotes.label: Exclusive Use
leaseNotes.value: No other premises in the SC > 15,000 SF for off-price brand-name men's/women's/children's apparel. Exceptions: TJ Maxx/Marshalls; Wal-Mart, Target, JCPenney, Sears, Kohl's (Alternate-Rent/termination mechanic if Kohl's opens) and other 50,000+ SF department stores; a full-line sporting-goods store; and pre-existing tenant rights.

leaseNotes.label: Co-tenancy
leaseNotes.value: If fewer than 3 of the named anchors are open for >30 days, Tenant pays Alternate Rent (lesser of 2% of sales or minimum rent); if the failure lasts >365 days, Tenant may terminate on 90 days' notice (or revert to full rent). Per the 2nd Amendment (§4), the named anchors are now King Soopers (~65,000 SF), ULTA (~9,744 SF, replacing Pier 1), Michaels (~32,000 SF), PetSmart (~15,000 SF), and Five Below (~10,000 SF, replacing 24 Hour Fitness). Qualified Replacement must use ≥80% of the replaced space and operate ≥25 stores regionally / 50 nationally. (Original Lease named Pier 1 and 24 Hour Fitness; the COVID exception no longer applies.)

leaseNotes.label: Kickout/Termination (LL)
leaseNotes.value: None

leaseNotes.label: Kickout/Termination (Tenant)
leaseNotes.value: None (co-tenancy termination right is captured under Co-tenancy)

leaseNotes.label: LL Restrictions
leaseNotes.value: The SC may not be used for: non-retail purposes; entertainment uses (bowling, skating, cinema, bar except incidental to a restaurant, nightclub, discotheque, amusement gallery, poolroom, health club except one existing + one small Curves-type ≤3,500 SF not adjacent to the Premises, massage parlor except Massage Envy/therapeutic ≤5,000 SF not contiguous, sports/game facility, off-track betting); pornographic materials (center-wide); used/second-hand goods (except first-class operators like Play It Again Sports ≤8,000 SF aggregate); educational facilities (except Huntington/Sylvan/Kaplan ≤5,000 SF aggregate, or Regency Beauty ≤7,500 SF); restaurants unless ≥150 ft from the Premises (existing ones grandfathered; aggregate ≤20,000 SF). Additional medical/dental ≤5,000 SF aggregate allowed.

leaseNotes.label: Tenant Restrictions
leaseNotes.value: Tenant will not use the Premises in violation of any other tenant's exclusive or prohibited use set forth in Schedule F. Schedule F binds the Premises to: (i) the recorded 1996 Declaration of Restrictions (~40 prohibited uses — entertainment, adult, automotive, mortuary, training/educational facility, etc.) and a 1998 Easement & Restrictive Covenant; and named-tenant restrictions for (ii) Beau Jo's Pizza (no nuisance/used-clothing/massage/cinema/recreation; certain uses within 125 ft of its premises need its consent), (iii) King Soopers/Kroger, (iv) Michaels, and prohibited-use carve-outs referencing (v) Office Max, (vi) PetSmart and (vii) Pier 1.

leaseNotes.label: CAM Method
leaseNotes.value: Pro-rata = Ground Floor Area of Premises ÷ Total Gross Leasable Area of the SC (service areas excluded). No admin fee. LL insurance, management/admin/overhead and capital expenditures excluded. CAP: 1st year ≤ $1.19/SF; thereafter increases ≤ 4%/yr non-cumulative (excluding snow removal and utility-rate increases). Audit within 3 years.

leaseNotes.label: Tax Method
leaseNotes.value: Pro-rata (same fraction as CAM). Separately-assessed out-parcels excluded from the denominator. Standard exclusions; no admin fee or cap. Initial estimate $3.73/SF. Tenant not required to pay until 20 days after receiving the bill + supporting documentation. Audit within 3 years.

leaseNotes.label: Insurance Method
leaseNotes.value: Landlord carries all-risk property + flood (excl. terrorism) at full replacement value on the Premises, and common-area CGL of $500K/person, $1M/occurrence, $100K property — naming Tenant as additional insured. Tenant reimburses its pro-rata share of the Annual Premium (same fraction as CAM), billed with CAM; no admin fee or cap; audit within 3 years. Tenant's own CGL is optional (if not carried, Tenant reimburses LL's CGL cost while Tenant's net worth is under $100M, §12.4). Mutual waiver of subrogation (§15.1).

leaseNotes.label: Assignment & Sublet
leaseNotes.value: No Landlord consent to assign or sublet the Premises; Landlord consent required to assign/sublet >25% of the floor area. Related-party transfers permitted without consent and without a Landlord termination right.

leaseNotes.label: Alterations
leaseNotes.value: Landlord consent required for alterations to the foundation, canopy, storefront, roof, exterior walls, or anything affecting structural integrity (except storefront changes consistent with the SC's uniform architectural design).

leaseNotes.label: Operating Covenant
leaseNotes.value: One day only (no continuing operating covenant).

leaseNotes.label: Go Dark Option
leaseNotes.value: Per the 2nd Amendment (replacing §4.8): closure for 180 consecutive days or more (after the 1st anniversary), other than for a Force Majeure Event, lets Landlord terminate on 30 days' notice; if Tenant gives a reopen notice it must reopen within 90 days. (Original §4.8 used 60 days.)

leaseNotes.label: Default
leaseNotes.value: Monetary default (§13.1): if Tenant fails to cure a rent/money default within 10 days after notice from Landlord, Landlord may send a termination notice and the term ends on the 5th day after that notice. Non-monetary default (§14.1 self-help): 30 days after notice (or longer if not curable in 30 days and Tenant diligently proceeds), after which Landlord may cure for Tenant's account. After any assignment, Landlord must give the default notice and cure opportunity to BOTH the original named tenant and the tenant in possession (§13.3). Interest on overdue amounts at Bank of America prime + 2% ('Default Rate', §13.6). No separate late fee. 2nd Amendment §5.4 adds a Forced-Shutdown rent-deferral mechanism (government-mandated closures) repaid over 12 months from the next Feb 1 / May 1, no interest or late fees.

leaseNotes.label: Guaranty
leaseNotes.value: None (Marshalls of MA, Inc., a TJX company, is the tenant).

leaseNotes.label: Outparcel Restrictions
leaseNotes.value: Out Parcels (labeled on the Lease Plan) may not exceed their presently existing building floor area or height collectively — except the new building on Unit 70 may be up to 27' and ~4,500 SF. The Prohibited Uses do not apply to Out Parcels except for noxious uses (bars, nightclubs, discotheques, massage parlors, off-track betting, pornography). If Units 71, 72 and/or 74 are acquired by Landlord they are deemed Out Parcels. Separately-assessed Out Parcels are excluded from the CAM/tax denominator.

leaseNotes.label: Purchase Option
leaseNotes.value: None — no purchase option or right of first refusal in the lease.

leaseNotes.label: Holdover
leaseNotes.value: Holdover minimum rent = 115% of the annual rate in effect immediately prior to expiration. Before Landlord accepts rent, holdover is a tenancy at sufferance; after acceptance, a month-to-month tenancy on the lease terms as applicable.

leaseNotes.label: Relocation
leaseNotes.value: None — Landlord has no right to relocate the Premises. The Control Area shown on the Lease Plan cannot be modified without Tenant's consent.

leaseNotes.label: Utilities
leaseNotes.value: Premises separately metered for each utility (electric, gas, water, sewer); Tenant pays its utilities directly. Shared fire riser valved/zoned by Landlord so the Premises' sprinkler water is separate. Landlord may interrupt utilities only in a bona-fide emergency with best efforts to minimize duration; rent abates during interruption and Tenant may terminate if it continues 3 consecutive days.

leaseNotes.label: HVAC
leaseNotes.value: Tenant maintains the HVAC serving the Premises and must keep a quarterly service/maintenance contract with a licensed contractor (copy to Landlord); if Tenant fails to maintain the contract, Landlord is not responsible for HVAC maintenance/repair/replacement. During the LAST 5 YEARS of the term, Landlord reimburses Tenant a prorated share of non-routine HVAC repairs/replacements (amortized over 120 months, or 60 months if the work occurs during an Extension Period), creditable against final rent. Landlord installed the original HVAC as part of Landlord's Construction Work.

leaseNotes.label: Pylon / Signage
leaseNotes.value: Tenant has the right to an identification panel on both sides of the Shopping Center pylon sign (its position is half of the former Office Max panel), plus exterior building signs (front and back) at maximum code letter height. If a future additional multi-tenant pylon is built, Tenant gets proportional billing. Landlord maintains the pylon; visibility may not be obstructed.

leaseNotes.label: Subordination / SNDA
leaseNotes.value: Tenant subordinates to future institutional mortgages ONLY if the mortgagee delivers a recordable non-disturbance/recognition agreement (Schedule D form) keeping the lease in force on foreclosure. Landlord owed Tenant an SNDA from the existing mortgagee within 60 days of lease execution (Sch B(8)).

leaseNotes.label: Estoppel
leaseNotes.value: Either party delivers an estoppel within 20 days of request (commencement/termination dates, in full force, no modifications/defaults). Landlord may request only in connection with a sale/refinance/transfer; Tenant only in connection with an assignment/sublease/equipment financing.

flags.issue: Base lease fully verified against the source 2015 document
flags.detail: Every base-lease term in this abstract was read from the full 6 MB 11/10/2015 lease (Articles I–XVIII + Schedules A–F), not just the workbook tab. Confirmed: minimum-rent ladder $16→$21/SF (which mathematically confirms GLA 22,821); four 5-year options; percentage rent at 2% over a NATURAL breakpoint (min rent ÷ .02); default (10-day money cure, prime+2%), holdover 115%, separately-metered utilities, tenant-maintained HVAC with last-5-years LL reimbursement, the off-price-apparel exclusive, CAM cap ($1.19/SF first year then ≤4%/yr, no admin/capital), and Schedule F third-party use restrictions. No radius, no purchase option, and no relocation right exist in the lease. The 2nd Amendment's 5th extension ($22/SF / $502,062) is internally consistent with the lease's $1/SF step pattern.

narrative: Marshalls (Marshalls of MA, Inc., a TJX company) occupies 22,821 SF (Suite 61) at University Hills, Denver under an 11/10/2015 lease that commenced 8/18/2016. Per the 5/30/2025 2nd Amendment, the Tenant exercised its 1st Extension, so the term now runs to 8/31/2031, with four more renewal options ($19–$22/SF) plus an Extra Period; current rent is $387,957/yr ($17/SF). The 2nd Amendment (with KPR now the landlord) also rewrote the co-tenancy — substituting ULTA for Pier 1 and Five Below for 24 Hour Fitness, curing the prior Pier-1 co-tenancy exposure — and replaced the go-dark trigger (60 → 180 days). The tenant holds a 15,000-SF off-price-apparel exclusive, a no-consent assignment right (consent only for >25% of the floor area), a tenant-favorable CAM cap ($1.19/SF first year then ≤4%/yr, no admin or capital costs), and a natural-breakpoint 2% percentage-rent clause. All base-lease terms in this abstract were verified against the full 11/10/2015 lease document; the only open items are the two review flags below — the on-file workbook tab predates the 2nd Amendment and should be updated, and the co-tenancy anchors changed.
